first.rationale: I intend to test a focused onboarding simplification because onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%, while prior evidence suggests onboarding changes can improve time-to-value and adoption. I will verify the onboarding, activation-messaging, and promotional-pricing records to distinguish a broad funnel problem from a pricing-specific threat before committing. A small guarded test should measure qualified activation and downstream conversion, not just completion, preserving uncertainty about whether pricing requires the next intervention.

final.rationale: Run a standard, guarded onboarding simplification experiment this week. Onboarding completion is down 4%, and the verified prior result shows a meaningful improvement in completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, directly addressing the current funnel deterioration while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Activation messaging is also credible, but onboarding is the more proximal issue and has the stronger retention evidence. Measure qualified activation, time-to-value, conversion, and 30-day retention—not completion alone. Do not use promotional pricing because its acquisition lift came with a 12% retention decline and is not sustainable.
